text:
sara_cs: Escalation from @acme — their rerank endpoint started returning identical / near-zero scores after a client library update. They say nothing else changed server-side. Threading this so eng can triage. payload snippet attached by customer below.

acme_dev: we rolled a client bump this morning. noticed rerank returns scores all 0.0 or 1.0 for everything (no ranking). example we sent: 
```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query": {"text": "best docs for onboarding"}, "documents": [{"id":"d1","content":"Onboarding steps","meta":{"query":{"text":"unexpected nested"}}}, {"id":"d2","content":"First-day checklist"}]}'```
we think the GraphQL client we use flattens nested objects into root keys and may be moving their `query` around.

sara_cs: customer provided server response — 200 OK but scores all the same. logs show a warning near parse time: "found nested `query` inside documents; using top-level query if present; nested queries ignored". They say they relied on nested query behaviour earlier (it used to work).

devon_engineering: @sara_cs thanks. quick hypotheses: 1) our parser historically accepted `documents[*].meta.query` as a signal (legacy) and silently promoted it to root query; 2) recent runtime change hardened parsing so only top-level `query` is used; 3) client flattening may have duplicated `query` keys causing ambiguous binding. Can you paste the full payload they send (raw bytes)?

acme_dev: here's raw (we scrubbed PII) — note our client library serializes nested objects with dot-keys: `{"documents.0.id":"d1","documents.0.content":"Onboarding steps","documents.0.meta.query.text":"unexpected nested","query.text":"best docs for onboarding"}` — so the server probably receives both top-level `query.text` and exploded `documents.0.meta.query.text`.

evan_support: reproducer I ran locally: send exploded-keys payload to rerank, server ends up reading the last-seen `query` key during naive header flattening and ends up with a root query value of `unexpected nested` while candidate extraction fails because `documents` array couldn't be reconstructed properly, so scores collapse. Quick test curl that reproduces: 
```bash
# reproducer that breaks ranking
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"documents.0.id":"d1","documents.0.content":"Onboarding steps","documents.0.meta.query.text":"foo","documents.1.id":"d2","documents.1.content":"First-day","query.text":"main query"}'
```
Result: 200 + body with `candidates: []` or candidates with default scores.

devon_engineering: thanks @evan_support — root cause confirmed: our request parsing layer accepts both normal JSON and form-encoded-like flattened keys when clients send content-type application/json but with exploded keys. Previously, a polyfill promoted nested query into the canonical `query` field during onboarding; we tightened that polyfill to avoid ambiguity. That change exposed the client bug.

sara_cs: acme says they can roll back client but need a short-term workaround — can we add a server-side compatibility check that reconstructs arrays from dot-keys OR at least returns a clear 422 with guidance? Right now it silently returns weird ranking.

devon_engineering: plan: (1) add explicit validation that requires `documents` or `candidates` to parse as arrays and return 422 with message "cannot parse documents: received flattened keys — please send proper JSON arrays or update client" (hotfix within 48h), (2) add a debug endpoint that echoes the parsed request shape for customers to verify, (3) longer-term: log a deprecation metric and follow up with client library patches. Filed RED-7894.

acme_dev: workaround worked — we moved their `query` to top-level and unflattened arrays on our side; ranking restored. Would appreciate the 422 and clearer error message so we can detect this in CI rather than in prod. :pray:

ops_deploy_bot: Roll scheduled: hotfix/parse-422 -> prod in ~2h (canary first).

sara_cs: Thanks team — forwarding update to customer and keeping thread open until rollout is live and they validate. +1 for the debug echo endpoint.

devon_engineering: follow-ups: add docs note in rerank API guide about not sending exploded/dotted keys; include example of allowed shapes for `documents`, `candidates`, and `passages` and prioritized query binding rules (root `query` wins, otherwise `query` in `candidates[i]` if unambiguous). I'll also add a short snippet showing a minimal valid payload: 
```json
{
  "query": { "text": "your query" },
  "candidates": [ { "id": "c1", "content": "..." }, { "id": "c2", "content": "..." } ]
}
```
we'll post the API doc patch after the hotfix.
